target.title: fix(codex): ignore empty mirrored session history
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server attempts can log `failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks` when harness hooks read a just-created mirrored session JSONL before the session header has been written.

In the observed gateway logs, the warning happened seconds before the corresponding session file's first record existed. Once the run finished, the same files parsed normally, which points to startup timing rather than corrupt session data.

## Why This Change Was Made

Missing mirrored history is already treated as empty history. An empty or whitespace-only mirrored session file is the same startup-race state: there is no history to replay yet, but there also is not a malformed transcript to warn about.

The change keeps malformed non-empty files returning `undefined`, so genuinely invalid history still surfaces through the existing warning path.

## User Impact

This reduces noisy Codex embedded-runtime warnings for normal new-session startup races without hiding real transcript corruption.

Operators should stop seeing repeated warning bursts for healthy cron sessions whose mirrored history file becomes valid shortly after startup.

## Evidence

- Local repro evidence from `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-07-03.log`: warning timestamps preceded the first JSONL session record by roughly `2.5s` to `20s`, while the same files later parsed successfully with `parseSessionEntries` / `buildSessionContext`.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-history.test.ts` passed with `6` tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `pnpm exec prettier --check ...` and `pnpm exec eslint ...` were attempted but those binaries are not available in this repo checkout; the commit hook ran formatting/checks for the touched files during commit.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Codex harness hook history reads should not warn when a mirrored session file exists but is still empty during a new-session startup race.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw gateway logs from `2026-07-03` under the user's active `~/.openclaw` state, plus the current source checkout.

Exact post-patch command/steps:

```bash
pnpm vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-history.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Evidence after fix: the new test writes a whitespace-only `session.jsonl` and verifies `readCodexMirroredSessionHistoryMessages()` returns `[]` instead of `undefined`; a separate test writes a non-empty malformed JSONL row and verifies it still returns `undefined` so the warning path remains available for real corruption.

Observed result: the targeted test file passed with `6` tests, including the new empty-file race coverage and malformed-file guard coverage.

What was not tested: a full live gateway run with a patched local OpenClaw install was not performed for this PR; the behavior is covered at the reader boundary that produces the warning condition.
